## Historical audit — S0038

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2/results/r1/fixed_h0/H0/development/commons_130842254/trajectory.jsonl`. References below are JSONL lines and supplied character ranges. This is a student trajectory, not a teacher-only trace.

| Evidence | Observation and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Student request, line 1 [0,5617) | The explicit goal was to reconstruct one indoor RGB photograph with separate meshes and matching viewpoint, framing, materials and occlusions. The image itself is not available for this audit. The student’s “historic stone kitchen” interpretation is an inference, not independently observed reference content. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3 [0,15060), 4 [0,15701) | The first program specified architecture, arches, a table, chimney, vessels, food and utensils, with colored materials, camera and lights. Its many separate components show intended multi-object construction, not verified spatial correctness. |
| Execution result, line 5 [0,1079) | Step 1 timed out after approximately 600 seconds with no image or diagnostic output: a **technical interruption**, not evidence of a particular geometric or algorithmic defect. |
| Student response and execution, lines 8 [0,18114), 9 [0,18755); result, line 10 [0,1984) | After receiving the timeout, the student replaced Boolean-heavy and individually modeled geometry with direct low-polygon meshes, combined paving, procedural noise/bump materials and lathed pottery. This is autonomous revision; whether any particular change caused the speed improvement is unproven. Step 2 failed because `sc.world` was `None`. |
| Student response and execution, lines 13 [0,17150), 14 [0,17790); results, lines 15 [0,41734), 16 [0,58) | The third program created a world when absent and revised tube construction. The runner reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file, and selected step 3. The code specifies multiple objects, procedural materials, separate handles and parts, object orientations, a camera and three area lights. Names and coordinates do not verify that parts touch correctly, poses or framing match, or lighting and textures look right. The log records 16 render samples despite the program requesting 24. |
| Student review, lines 17 [0,100867), 18 [0,3326), 19 [0,340) | The reference and final render were supplied to the student’s review call; the student answered `DONE`. No visual diagnosis or independent comparison is recorded, and no execution budget remained. |

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Formal execution succeeded and a build was selected after two failed attempts; reconstruction accuracy remains **unknown**, not established success or partial correctness. Neither image is visible in the supplied audit text, so multiple objects in the reference, connections, pose, camera, lighting and render defects cannot be independently checked. The timeout’s cause remains unresolved. No teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption appears in this trace; runner error feedback is not teacher input.

**Transferable observation:** runtime feedback can support targeted recovery, as the missing-world guard followed the explicit exception. **Task-specific observation:** the kitchen geometry, viewpoint and surface choices remain unverified hypotheses about this particular photograph.
